subject: Marketplace Kickstart: Hero copy, SKU naming, private-offer flow
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@amazon.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@dataco.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro & Marketplace listing kickoff for DataCo / Redwood

Hi Ava —

Quick intro: DataCo is moving forward on an integration with Redwood for an inference offering they want to list on AWS Marketplace (SaaS). I'm the AWS listing rep on the account. DataCo's procurement asked if we can kick off the listing setup and confirm co-sell requirements so mutual teams can align on timelines.

Key asks from AWS/DataCo: 
- Confirm whether this will be a SaaS listing (recommended) versus AMI/EC2, and what artifacts we need.
- A short hero paragraph + 2–3 feature bullets optimized for the Marketplace product page.
- SKU / entitlement mapping for private offers and usage-based pricing notes.
- Any legal/procurement items (tax/VAT footnotes, terms) that will affect PO.

Can we schedule a 30m sync this week? DataCo is in the Pacific timezone and prefers mornings. I've included their procurement contact.

Thanks,
Sophie
Amazon Web Services — Marketplace Partner Development
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@amazon.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@dataco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & Marketplace listing kickoff for DataCo / Redwood

Thanks Sophie — happy to kick this off. Looping in Ben (marketplace lead), Karthik (product/legal), and Lauren (partner ops) to help scope deliverables.

Short answers up front:
- We recommend a SaaS (hosted) listing in Marketplace. No AMI required for Redwood-hosted inference; AMI/EC2 applies to self-hosted offerings only.
- I'll attach a draft product page (hero + bullets) and a preliminary SKU mapping CSV for private-offer entitlements.

Proposed next steps / timeline: 
1) Quick 30m call (this week) to confirm DataCo's procurement requirements and private-offer cadence.
2) We finalize hero + bullets and share draft product page for AWS review (2 business days).
3) Ben and Karthik finalize SKU prefixes + footnotes; Lauren coordinates DocuSign/private-offer template.

I'm attaching a first-pass draft product page and SKU map for your review. Specific asks for the call: 
- DataCo to confirm expected billing cadence and whether they need usage metering at the org or account level.
- AWS to confirm co-sell opt-in process and any required collateral for their sales motions.

Attachments: product_page_draft_v1.pdf; sku_mapping.csv

Proposed times: Wed 5/26 11:00–11:30 PT or Thu 5/27 09:00–09:30 PT. Let me know what works for you.

Best,
Ava Chen
Director, GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@amazon.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@dataco.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & Marketplace listing kickoff for DataCo / Redwood

Nice kickoff — I reviewed the draft product page and left inline suggestions on tone and CTAs. High-level notes here to feed into the call: 

Hero messaging: 
- Keep headline customer-centric: "Predictable, low-latency LLM inference for production apps" (short).
- Subhead: 1–2 lines that highlight predictable pricing and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Lead with measurable outcomes (lower per-token cost via caching/quantization, SLA-backed latency) — saves buyer time to evaluate.

Feature bullets (recommend 3): 
1) Fast, consistent inference: <30ms p50 for typical seqs on hosted instances.
2) Cost controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce unit costs.
3) Enterprise ready: VPC/private deployments, KMS integration, and SLA-backed Dedicated capacity.

Pricing footnote guidance: avoid committing to strict per-token numbers on the page; instead link to pricing tiers and add: "Contact us for private-offer pricing and committed throughput discounts." That stays flexible for DataCo's private offer.

SKU / Entitlements: 
- Recommend SKU prefix: REDW-ML-INF- (keeps it simple). Use trailing qualifiers for tier and region (eg REDW-ML-INF-STND-US).
- For private offers, we need mapping from SKU -> entitlement units and a clear billing metric (tokens vs request units). I'll own the final CSV.

Operational asks for DataCo on the call: expected monthly committed units, whether they require org-level metering, and if they need volume discounts baked into the PO.

Links: HubSpot deal HS-98765; shared drive with product page draft: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-product-page-draft

I'll be on the call Weds 11a PT.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Marketing Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@amazon.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@dataco.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & Marketplace listing kickoff for DataCo / Redwood

A couple legal/technical clarifications from my side after reviewing the draft and Ben's notes: 

1) AMI vs SaaS: Confirming Ava's note — SaaS listing is correct. If DataCo needed to self-host via AMI, we'd need to certify an AMI and provide support docs. For hosted SaaS we will not publish AMIs.

2) SKU naming: REDW-ML-INF- is fine. Please ensure SKU descriptions in the CSV include both the billing metric and the region qualifier; that reduces later mapping confusion during private-offer creation.

3) Terms & footnotes: Add a short legal footnote on the product page: "Offer subject to Redwood Inference Master SaaS Terms; private offers governed by executed PO and AWS private-offer process." That keeps the page concise while protecting terms.

4) Attachments: I'll upload a legal checklist and the private-offer template (aws_private_offer_template.docx) and a marketplace readiness checklist (marketplace_checklist.xlsx). Ben, please confirm the final SKU mapping CSV before we hand to AWS.

I'll join the call and can field procurement questions on invoicing, tax treatment, and PO language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Product & GTM | Redwood Inference
